pool.sol: The Inscribed Angle Theorem states that the measure of an inscribed angle is always half the measure of the central angle subtending the same arc: \( \theta_{\text{inscribed}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\theta_{\text{central}} \).

pool.text: In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure \(14^\circ\) and \(10^\circ\). What is the measure of the exterior angle at the third vertex?
pool.sol: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, the exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: \(14+10=24^\circ\).

pool.text: Can segments of length 10, 12, and 12 form a triangle?
choices: Only if the triangle is isosceles
No, they cannot form a triangle
Yes, they can form a triangle
Only if the triangle is right
pool.sol: Triangle Inequality Theorem: the sum of any two sides must exceed the third. \(10+12=22>12\), \(10+12=22>12\), \(12+12=24>10\), so yes.

pool.text: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle A = 42^\circ\) and \(\angle B = 68^\circ\). In \(\triangle DEF\), \(\angle D = 70^\circ\) and \(\angle E = 68^\circ\). Which statement correctly determines whether the triangles are similar?
choices: The triangles are similar by AA because \(\angle C = 70^\circ\), matching \(\angle D\)
The triangles are not similar because \(\angle A \neq \angle D\)
The triangles are similar by SAS using sides adjacent to \(68^\circ\)
Similarity cannot be determined without side lengths
pool.sol: In \(\triangle ABC\), the interior angles sum to \(180^\circ\): \(\angle C = 180^\circ - 42^\circ - 68^\circ = 70^\circ\). In \(\triangle DEF\), two angles are \(68^\circ\) and \(70^\circ\). Both triangles share angles of \(68^\circ\) and \(70^\circ\). By the Angle-Angle (AA) Similarity Postulate, \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle FED\).

pool.text: \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\) are shown below with \(\angle A \cong \angle D = 55^\circ\). If \(AB = 6\), \(AC = 10\), \(DE = 9\), and \(DF = 15\), which similarity criterion applies and what is the scale factor from \(\triangle ABC\) to \(\triangle DEF\)?
choices: The triangles are not similar because side \(BC\) is unknown
pool.sol: Check the ratio of corresponding sides adjacent to the congruent included angle: \(\frac{DE}{AB} = \frac{9}{6} = 1.5\) and \(\frac{DF}{AC} = \frac{15}{10} = 1.5\). Since two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same constant ratio and their included angles are congruent (\(\angle A \cong \angle D\)), \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF\) by SAS similarity with scale factor \(k = 1.5\).

pool.text: Which of the following conditions is NOT sufficient to prove that two triangles are similar?
choices: Two pairs of corresponding angles are congruent (AA)
Three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional (SSS)
Two pairs of sides are proportional and a non-included angle is congruent (SSA)
Two pairs of sides are proportional and their included angle is congruent (SAS)
pool.sol: SSA (Side-Side-Angle) is NOT a valid similarity criterion. When the congruent angle is not included between the proportional sides, the third side can swing to form two non-congruent, non-similar triangles (the ambiguous case). In contrast, AA, SAS, and SSS all rigorously guarantee triangle similarity.

pool.text: The sides of \(\triangle ABC\) measure \(7\), \(10\), and \(12\). A similar triangle \(\triangle DEF\) has a shortest side of length \(21\). What is the perimeter of \(\triangle DEF\)?
pool.sol: The shortest side of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(7\). The corresponding shortest side of \(\triangle DEF\) is \(21\). The linear scale factor is \(k = \frac{21}{7} = 3\). The perimeter of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(P_1 = 7 + 10 + 12 = 29\). Since perimeters scale linearly by \(k\), the perimeter of \(\triangle DEF\) is \(P_2 = 3 \times 29 = 87\).

pool.text: Trapezoid \(ABCD\) has parallel bases \(AB = 6\) and \(CD = 14\). The diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at point \(P\). What is the ratio of \(\text{Area}(\triangle APB)\) to \(\text{Area}(\triangle CPD)\)?

The linear scale factor is \(k = \frac{AB}{CD} = \frac{6}{14} = \frac{3}{7}\). pool.text: In trapezoid \(ABCD\) with \(AB \parallel CD\), \(AB = 8\) and \(CD = 12\). The diagonals intersect at \(P\). If the entire diagonal \(AC = 30\), what is the length of segment \(AP\)?
pool.sol: Because \(\triangle APB \sim \triangle CPD\), corresponding segments along the diagonal satisfy \(\frac{AP}{PC} = \frac{AB}{CD} = \frac{8}{12} = \frac{2}{3}\). The total length is \(AC = AP + PC = 30\). Thus, \(AP = 30 \times \frac{2}{2+3} = 30 \times \frac{2}{5} = 12\) (and \(PC = 18\)).

pool.text: Chords \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect inside a circle at point \(P\). If \(PA = 4\), \(PB = 9\), and \(PC = 6\), what is the length of segment \(PD\)?

pool.text: Chords \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersect inside a circle at point \(P\). The segments on chord \(AB\) measure \(PA = x\) and \(PB = x + 7\). The segments on chord \(CD\) measure \(PC = 3\) and \(PD = 6\). What is the total length of chord \(AB\)?
pool.sol: By the Intersecting Chords Theorem: \(PA \cdot PB = PC \cdot PD \implies x(x + 7) = 3 \times 6 = 18 \implies x^2 + 7x - 18 = 0\). Factoring: \((x + 9)(x - 2) = 0\). Since length must be positive, \(x = 2\). Therefore, \(PA = 2\) and \(PB = 2 + 7 = 9\). The total length of chord \(AB = PA + PB = 2 + 9 = 11\).

pool.text: From an external point \(P\), a tangent segment \(PT\) touches a circle at \(T\), and a secant line passes through the circle intersecting it at \(A\) and \(B\) with \(PA = 9\). If tangent \(PT = 12\), what is the length of chord \(AB\)?
pool.sol: By the Tangent-Secant Theorem (derived from similar triangles \(\triangle PTA \sim \triangle PBT\)): \(PT^2 = PA \cdot PB\). Substituting: \(12^2 = 9 \cdot PB \implies 144 = 9 \cdot PB \implies PB = 16\). The chord length is \(AB = PB - PA = 16 - 9 = 7\).

pool.text: In a circle with chords \(AB\) and \(CD\) intersecting at \(P\), which reason rigorously proves that \(\triangle PAC \sim \triangle PDB\)?

pool.text: The diagonals of trapezoid \(ABCD\) with \(AB \parallel CD\) intersect at \(P\). If \(\text{Area}(\triangle APB) = 16\) and \(\text{Area}(\triangle CPD) = 49\), what is the total area of trapezoid \(ABCD\)?
pool.sol: Because \(\triangle APB \sim \triangle CPD\), the ratio of areas is \(16/49 = (4/7)^2\). For any trapezoid, the side triangles have equal area given by the geometric mean of the base triangles: \(\text{Area}(\triangle APD) = \text{Area}(\triangle BPC) = \sqrt{16 \times 49} = 4 \times 7 = 28\). The total area of the trapezoid is \(16 + 49 + 28 + 28 = 121\) (which equals \((4 + 7)^2 = 11^2 = 121\)).

pool.text: In the figure below, lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) are parallel with \(AB = 10\) and \(CD = 15\). Segments \(AD\) and \(BC\) intersect at point \(E\). If the perimeter of \(\triangle ABE\) is \(26\), what is the perimeter of \(\triangle CDE\)?

pool.text: In \(\triangle JKL\) with right angle at vertex \(K\), an altitude from \(K\) meets hypotenuse \(JL\) at point \(M\). Given that segment \(JM = 5\) and \(ML = 15\), determine the length of leg \(JK\).
pool.sol: By the Geometric Mean Leg Theorem (projection theorem): \(JK^2 = JM \cdot JL\). The full hypotenuse is \(JL = JM + ML = 5 + 15 = 20\). Therefore, \(JK^2 = 5 \times 20 = 100 \implies JK = \sqrt{100} = 10\).

pool.text: In \(\triangle ABC\), ray \(AD\) bisects \(\angle BAC\) with \(D\) lying on side \(BC\). If \(AB = x + 3\), \(AC = 2x\), \(BD = 4\), and \(DC = 6\), what is the value of \(x\)?
pool.sol: By the Angle Bisector Theorem, the ratio of the divided base segments equals the ratio of the adjacent sides: \(\frac{BD}{DC} = \frac{AB}{AC} \implies \frac{4}{6} = \frac{x + 3}{2x}\). Cross-multiplying: \(4(2x) = 6(x + 3) \implies 8x = 6x + 18 \implies 2x = 18 \implies x = 9\).

pool.text: In \(\triangle ABC\), a transversal segment \(DE\) connects side \(AB\) at \(D\) and side \(AC\) at \(E\) such that \(\angle ADE = \angle C\). If \(AD = 3\), \(AC = 9\), and the area of \(\triangle ADE\) is \(8\), what is the area of quadrilateral \(BDEC\)?
pool.sol: Because \(\angle ADE = \angle C\) and both triangles share \(\angle A\), \(\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ACB\) by AA. The linear scale factor from the small triangle to the large triangle is \(k = \frac{AC}{AD} = \frac{9}{3} = 3\). The ratio of their areas is \(k^2 = 3^2 = 9\). Thus, \(\text{Area}(\triangle ABC) = 9 \times \text{Area}(\triangle ADE) = 9 \times 8 = 72\). The area of quadrilateral \(BDEC = \text{Area}(\triangle ABC) - \text{Area}(\triangle ADE) = 72 - 8 = 64\).

pool.text: A student whose eyes are \(1.5\text{ m}\) above the ground places a mirror flat on the ground \(2\text{ m}\) in front of her feet.
